problem.title: Prior Auth Session Cycle Time Analysis
problem.prompt: A prior authorization tracking system logs each status change event for authorization requests. Clinical staff often work on multiple requests in discrete work sessions separated by breaks. You need to group each staff member's events into sessions, where a new session starts if more than 20 minutes have elapsed since their previous event. Calculate the cycle time (duration from first to last event) for each session that contains at least 2 events. A session is defined per staff member: events from different staff members are always in separate sessions, even if timestamps overlap. Return columns `staff_member_id`, `session_id` (a sequential number per staff member, starting at 1 for their earliest session), and `cycle_time_minutes` (the difference in minutes between the session's last and first event timestamp, rounded to 2 decimal places). Order results by `staff_member_id`, then `session_id`.
problem.schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE auth_events (event_id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, staff_member_id INT NOT NULL, payer_auth_request_id VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL, event_timestamp TIMESTAMP NOT NULL, status_code VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL);

composite_moves: CTE 1: LAG(event_timestamp) OVER (PARTITION BY staff_member_id ORDER BY event_timestamp) to get previous_ts per staff member
CTE 1: CASE WHEN previous_ts IS NULL OR event_timestamp - previous_ts > INTERVAL '20 minutes' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END as new_session_flag
CTE 2: SUM(new_session_flag) OVER (PARTITION BY staff_member_id ORDER BY event_timestamp ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) as session_id
GROUP BY staff_member_id, session_id with HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2
Aggregate: ROUND(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM MAX(event_timestamp) - MIN(event_timestamp)) / 60, 2) as cycle_time_minutes

hints: Consider how to identify when a new work session begins for each staff member based on time gaps between consecutive events.
Use LAG() to compare each event's timestamp with the previous event's timestamp for the same staff member, then flag rows where the gap exceeds 20 minutes or is the first event.

After flagging session boundaries, use a cumulative SUM() over the flags to assign a sequential session_id per staff member, then group by staff_member_id and session_id to calculate the time span from MIN to MAX event timestamp within each session, filtering for sessions with at least 2 events.
problem.answer_key: WITH event_gaps AS (SELECT staff_member_id, event_timestamp, LAG(event_timestamp) OVER (PARTITION BY staff_member_id ORDER BY event_timestamp) AS previous_ts, CASE WHEN LAG(event_timestamp) OVER (PARTITION BY staff_member_id ORDER BY event_timestamp) IS NULL OR event_timestamp - LAG(event_timestamp) OVER (PARTITION BY staff_member_id ORDER BY event_timestamp) > INTERVAL '20 minutes' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS new_session_flag FROM auth_events), sessions AS (SELECT staff_member_id, event_timestamp, SUM(new_session_flag) OVER (PARTITION BY staff_member_id ORDER BY event_timestamp ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS session_id FROM event_gaps) SELECT staff_member_id, session_id, ROUND(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM MAX(event_timestamp) - MIN(event_timestamp)) / 60, 2) AS cycle_time_minutes FROM sessions GROUP BY staff_member_id, session_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2 ORDER BY staff_member_id, session_id;

_meta.scenario: a prior authorization cycle time tracking system across payers

user_solution:
/* notes */
WITH add_prev_time AS (
    SELECT
        staff_member_id,
        event_timestamp,
        LAG(event_timestamp) OVER (PARTITION BY staff_member_id ORDER BY event_timestamp) AS prev_ts
    FROM auth_events
),
flag_new_session as (
    SELECT
        staff_member_id,
        event_timestamp,
        CASE 
            WHEN prev_ts IS NULL OR
                 event_timestamp - prev_ts > INTERVAL '20 minutes' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_new_session
    FROM add_prev_time

),
assign_session_id AS (
    SELECT
        staff_member_id,
        event_timestamp,
        SUM(is_new_session) OVER (PARTITION BY staff_member_id ORDER BY event_timestamp) AS session_id
    FROM flag_new_session

)
SELECT
    staff_member_id, 
    session_id,
    ROUND( 
        EXTRACT(
            EPOCH FROM (MAX(event_timestamp) - MIN(event_timestamp)) / 60
        )
    ,2) AS cycle_time_minutes
FROM assign_session_id
GROUP BY staff_member_id, session_id
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2
ORDER BY 1;
